## Design

### 2026-11-01: ![wiring](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/5cf10048d64afed6d9dd95efd86010fd02f83254ee8029e6218935f891cbf1ac.png)

**3h**

![wiring](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/5cf10048d64afed6d9dd95efd86010fd02f83254ee8029e6218935f891cbf1ac.png)
I started working on the schematic. I'm going to be using a Raspberry Pi Pico and a TFT display, which I just put into an 8-pin header. The wiring wasn't as bad as some of the other projects.

![betterwiring](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/e18d7acf28442f0f63e7e1b939ae139a9253907b248023ca2a71b37203852818.png)
I realized after wiring everything up that I could flip the orientation of the 8-pin header, so I flipped it, and now there are much fewer wires overlapping each other, and everything looks much cleaner.

![pcb](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/0a55933976e56e796377d848f5da239010b7a328cf91dc6c5ac72128724224df.png)
I then chose the footprints for each component and put them into the PCB designer. This part was easier than the schematic, since all of the ratlines were already in place. I just connected all of them and made a back-layer copper fill to ground all of the necessary connections.

### 2026-11-01: In this session, I worked on the software side of things. In order for my project to work, I needed to write two separate pieces of code, one for the computer and the other for the Raspberry Pi Pico.

**4h**

In this session, I worked on the software side of things. In order for my project to work, I needed to write two separate pieces of code, one for the computer and the other for the Raspberry Pi Pico.

![codesetup](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/844cd4af06cf7d62fbc2f35eef9ef022f4cb8233de333cc5c9aa5879070062f1.png)
This is the beginning part of the code for the computer. It imports the necessary things to retrieve data about the computer. The psutil library allows the code to get data about the CPU and RAM.

![pccode](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/f0c3bf583f49f74e5f0b6b2e29010ff3038fb2f6e6702625271a0766aee6da8c.png)
The rest of the code sets the initial data to 0 as a placeholder until the data gets here. Then, in a loop, it constantly imports data, updates it, and then puts it into an organized list. That is then sent to the raspberry pico.

![codesetup2](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/8b75a4ca06d4fd70d3578faf7b9c42a85709bcf4c43ee7858e7374a4c949b653.png)
This is for the Raspberry Pi. It again imports the necessary things in order to read the data from the computer. It also resets the display and gets it ready to update.

![picocode](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/72736e371ee42d5484ddd2407e39d98c6f37cf672f6454aad9ec41e255355353.png)

This is another loop that takes in an incoming data string and separates it back into 5 different texts, then prints it on the display.
